classification.difficultyReason: Convert whole and half tree symbols using the key, total the farm frequencies, and use that total to calculate each requested percentage.

content.prompt: The pictogram below shows the numbers of trees grown on each of four neighbouring tree farms.

spec.description: Four aligned labelled rows with equally sized tree outlines. Counts are 5½, 4½, 3½ and 4½; every final half-symbol is the left half of the same tree. Decorative green fills are omitted under house style.
spec.mathematics: One whole tree symbol represents 1000 trees. North Pole: 5500; Santa's: 4500; Christmas: 3500; Pines: 4500.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source symbols, farm labels and key are supplied; numerical frequencies remain student responses.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many trees are grown on Santa’s Tree Farm?

children.label: b
children.prompt: How many trees are grown in total?

children.label: c
children.prompt: What percentage of the trees is grown at the Pines Tree Farm?

children.label: d
children.prompt: What percentage, to the nearest per cent, of the trees is grown at the North Pole Tree Farm?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage}&=\frac{5500}{18\,000}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage}&=30\frac{5}{9}\%\\\text{Percentage}&\approx31\%\end{aligned}$$
To the nearest per cent, 31% of the trees are grown at the North Pole Tree Farm.
